context.requirement_text: REQ-205 -- S7 scenario-harness foundation: Elixir scenario runner, business-tenant fixture seeding, and the API-vs-GUI execution split. See docs/requirements.yaml id: REQ-205 for full text and 8 acceptance_criteria.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: test/fixtures/simulation/{swiftroute,vortex,meridian}/ contains all 12 company/org/process YAML files ported from R-Co's tests/simulation/companies/, with actor_id values unchanged from the R-Co originals -- verified by a diff-style comparison test
AC2: Letflow.Simulation.Seed provisions all three companies' tenant, users, groups and process definitions by calling Letflow's own context modules directly (no HTTP client, no Python subprocess)
AC3: seeding the same company twice in one test run is a no-op the second time -- one explicit test per entity kind
AC4: Letflow.Simulation.Runner executes a minimal one-step api-via scenario end to end against a real running instance and evaluates at least one instance_state-method expected outcome
AC5: a scenario step declared via: gui is recorded with outcome DEFERRED_TO_S8, never silently skipped, never executed as an api step
AC6: the runner moduledoc distinguishes this harness from Letflow.Routers.SimulationTest/simulation_test.zig, states this requirement does not build that router, cites both R-Co source files by path
AC7: if a YAML-parsing library is added to mix.exs, REVIEWER sign-off is recorded for it
AC8: mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

task.description: RELEASE-VALIDATOR pass (WF-02 Step 5) for REQ-205 -- independently re-verify all 8 acceptance criteria against current source and re-run tests, and make the primary AC1 accept/reject decision the run's own gates deferred (ELIXIR-DEV found R-Co source at c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co\ genuinely unreachable from this Linux sandbox and substituted disclosed synthetic fixture content; SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER/TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR/TEST-RUNNER all confirmed the disclosure is honest and deferred the accept/reject call to this step).

ac1_decision.verdict: ACCEPT WITH RECORDED CAVEAT -- does not block REQ-205 being marked done
ac1_decision.reachability_reverified_independently: No /mnt/c or Windows-host mount; find / -xdev for swiftroute/vortex/meridian content (excluding this repo's own now-existing fixtures) returns nothing; no sibling-session artifact in this repo carries the real content. This sandbox DOES have outbound network reachability (confirmed: ICMP + raw TCP connect both succeed) but that is irrelevant -- there is no address/credential anywhere in this repo for the specific Windows host at c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co\. Confirmed genuinely unreachable from this sandbox, same conclusion as ELIXIR-DEV, independently re-derived rather than trusted.
ac1_decision.key_observation: docs/requirements.yaml's own REQ-205 description states the source material was 'confirmed present in R-Co ... this session' at requirement-drafting time -- meaning some session/host DID have R-Co filesystem access when REQ-ANALYST wrote this requirement. This makes AC1's gap a routing problem (dispatch the fixture-porting work to a host with R-Co access), not a permanently-lost-data problem.
ac1_decision.rest_of_requirement_stands_independently: Yes -- Letflow.Simulation.Seed and Letflow.Simulation.Runner depend only on the fixture YAML's shape (slug/display_name/hostname, people/groups with actor_id, name/version/graph), never on specific R-Co values -- confirmed by reading both modules directly, no hardcoded synthetic values found outside the fixture files themselves. Swapping the 12 files for real R-Co content later is a data-only change with zero code change required.
ac1_decision.precedent: None found for 'real content unavailable, structurally-equivalent synthetic substituted, explicitly disclosed' in this session. REQ-202's design doc records the same environmental constraint (R-Co unreachable) but a different resolution -- REQ-202's requirement text already had the needed facts pre-verified/recorded at drafting time, so no fresh file access was needed. REQ-205's AC1 needed literal byte-for-byte content never transcribed anywhere. This is a novel resolution for this session, not a repeat of an already-accepted pattern -- flagging it as the precedent going forward, not citing one.
ac1_decision.consequence_for_req206_207_208: REQ-206/207/208 run real R-Co scenario YAML referencing specific actor_id values (e.g. actor-swiftroute-lena) expected to resolve against REQ-205's org/company fixtures. Against the current SYNTHETIC fixtures, those real actor references will not resolve -- REQ-206 cannot be genuinely run against real R-Co scenario content until REQ-205's 12 fixture files are the real, actor-id-matching ones. This is a hard blocking prerequisite for REQ-206, not a deferrable cleanup.
ac1_decision.recommendation_to_orch: File a follow-up task (RELEASE-VALIDATOR does not self-file per ISSUE_QUEUE.md -- routing is ORCH's job): port REQ-205's 12 R-Co company/org/process fixture files with real content and unchanged actor_id values, on a host with c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co\ access, and make it a hard depends_on prerequisite of REQ-206 starting. Scope is small: only test/fixtures/simulation/**/*.yaml changes; zero test/support/simulation/{seed,runner}.ex changes required per ELIXIR-DEV's own note, re-confirmed by this step.
ac1_decision.doc_updater_instructions: Record REQ-205 status as done, but its acceptance-criteria record must show AC1 as PARTIALLY MET (structure/mechanism/test genuinely met; literal 'ported from R-Co with actor_id values unchanged' content NOT met -- synthetic substitute in place, disclosed in every fixture file's header comment), not a blanket 'all 8 ACs met.' Cross-reference the follow-up fixture-porting task once ORCH files it.
